question: Do info, verify (with and without --decode), emdf, oamd and au read a stream on standard input once, in memory that does not grow with the stream, and report what they report of a file of the same bytes? What does reading it once cost in time?
method: The commands take `-` through `pipeline::Pass`: the head (64 KiB) tells the codecs apart, the stream is framed by the framer a walk over a file uses and every unit is lent to the walk of the command and, for emdf and oamd, to the checks of verify. The equality of reports is held by tests on every fixture and every stream of tests/found: cli_stdin.rs (text, --json and exit code of the five commands, file against pipe) and oadec-engine/tests/pipeline.rs (api::*_from against the calls of a Source, pieces cut anywhere, a stream cut inside a unit, a read that fails, a stream entered between major syncs). Peak memory is read from the system while the command waits for the end of a pipe into which everything was written: PeakWorkingSet64 on Windows. Wall time is the least of three runs of each command on the same stream as a file and as a pipe. Debug builds (cargo test profile), Windows 11, a 28-thread machine shared with other jobs; not the measurement of gate 3, which is tools/bench.py on a release build with nothing else running.

peak_memory_mib.unexplained: info of the longest stream held 17.6 MiB where verify, which makes the same scan, held 11.8; at 160 MiB both held 12.2. One sample each.

wall_seconds_file_against_pipe.not_met: emdf and oamd of an E-AC-3 stream take 1.87 times as long piped in as from the file: the file is walked twice on two threads, the checks of verify beside the walk; a pipe is read once on one thread, and the checks of an E-AC-3 stream parse every frame to its last bit. Not measured in a release build.

not_measured: the time of the file path before and after (tools/bench.py)
